notes.title: Update to version 1.0.2
notes.notes:
Hola, amig@s!

In this small 1.0.2 update we squashed some bugs and improved menu handling in pause:

[list]
[*] BUG - minor - when jumping on dialog init with NPCs char can stuck in the ground blocking other actions
[*] BUG - trivial - jumping on dialogue start may not display the very first message
[*] BUG - medium - when rushing through the objects in powerup mode char can be killed by the objects
[*] UI - reduce navigation delay in the pause menu
[*] Extra - entering dialogue mode with NPCs is improved
[/list]

notes.title: Contest time!

The rules of this contest are very simple. It's time to activate your creativity! 
[b]What would one of our characters say to our spiky hero? And what would be the answer? [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35457696/a99edcaacf3ed1bd1b88cdb6782d12ae8043ca24.png[/img]

notes.title: Flippin Kaktus Steam Playtest is Here!
notes.notes:
We are at an exciting time where we are almost ready for people to get a closer look at Flippin Kaktus!

Our game has now been accepted onto the Steam Playtest feature. In light of this, we have decided to gather some feedback about gameplay, mechanics, and level design so that we can adjust it before the release..

If you are a fan of action-filled side-scrolling run-and-gun types of games we invite you to sign up for the playtest of the latest version of the game Playtest feature TODAY! 
From the 9st December, we will be granting access to a small group of you in order to get as much info about the game as possible. We will use this time to incorporate some fixes, and adjust the gameplay so that the game will shine!

After playing the game you’ll be asked to do a quick survey - please fill in all the details and give us as much as you can - it will help the game, we promise :)  

Any further questions, please feel free to join the community discussion over in our Discord channel. Check out the Steam Playtest Q&A below for more details about it.

[h1]Steam Playtest Q&A[/h1]

[i][b]So what is Steam Playtest and how does it work?[/b][/i]
The Steam Playtest feature allows anyone interested in trying out Flippin Kaktus to enroll onto a list of playtesters from the Steam store page.

Once enrolled, we will be giving playtesters access to the game in batches starting today. Steam will alert you once you have been accepted. Once you have been granted access, you will be able to play the full latest version of the game without any time limits for as long as we decide to run the playtest.
[i]
[b]How do I enroll as a playtester?[/b][/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35457696/f7e0e2674c1375b02aa24fe61dc800e3a24f88d3.jpg[/img]
Visit the Flippin Kaktus page and you will find the option to enroll in the same location as the purchase button. Click the button to sign up and you’re all set. Once Steam notifies you that you have access, the game will be available to download in your library.

You’ll also find the form for feedback here! 
[url=https://forms.gle/dJ9omojQr8EkDjsk9]https://forms.gle/dJ9omojQr8EkDjsk9[/url]

notes.title: Flippin Kaktus pokes its way into the Indie Cup Event! + Screenshot Contest
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35457696/be34cdd6691986690a8a72f61989c3318afd4e3e.png[/img]

[h1]Hello, my cacti with or without black ties![/h1]

First things first, I have to thank all of you for wishlisting the game here on Steam and for leaving feedback through the various top-or-not secret channels. B[b]oth of these things not only help me reach more people to share my labor of love with but also let me know that there are people out there who care![/b] They care about something I made! It still feels crazy to this day, and I am so grateful to all of you for this crazy feeling, may it never go away.

Now then, [i]vamos al grano[/i], as they say. Today I’m happy to announce that [b]Flippin Kaktus[/b] is taking part in the [b]Indie Cup Event[/b] on Steam that runs from 7th to 11th of October (aka it starts now!). I’m so excited for my game to reach more people, and I’m honored to participate in this competition. I hope I can count on your support and that you will cheer me and Flippin on in this contest.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35457696/d1b3d2ef0f40f3be2eaa0cd68b4f23b86a1e9742.png[/img]

[h2]Screenshot Contest[/h2]

Now, with that out of the way, I can share with you some other awesome news. We’re running a [b]Screenshot Contest[/b] in which you can win a FREE key to Flippin Kaktus on the day of release!

[b]What should I do?[/b]
1. Download the demo [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1119010/Flippin_Kaktus/]here[/url]!
2. Take a cool and amazing screenshot by Steam overlay (default - click F12).
3. Make it public by clicking Views -> Screenshots and click “Upload” below your beautiful screenshot.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35457696/cc08ab19462e7db662663fa9b0a211d273e6b4e8.png[/img]

[b]4. Now all you need to do is to click “View Online”, copy the link to your screenshot and share it [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1119010/discussions/0/3079890849088747547/]HERE[/url].[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35457696/f22cc8a6bc7c04076659e45f3cc09f2fd136f83f.png[/img]

You have time until [b]October 13[/b], we’ll announce the winner shortly after. Hope you’ll participate, and have fun doing so! Don’t let the kaktus sting you. ;)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35457696/43f19112ac96bb4f11016306723de7c420d2b2d0.png[/img]

That's all I’ve had to say for this announcement. If you haven’t played the demo yet - try it, if you have - leave some feedback here on the forums. I intently read and appreciate every single comment, even (or especially) the negative ones! It helps the game evolve, grow and improve and when the game improves - I improve. If you could also click that wishlist button, I cannot stress enough how much it helps with the game’s discoverability. And the more people discover it, the more will try the demo and leave feedback!

[b]Thank you for reading, and have a nice day, friends![/b]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1119010/Flippin_Kaktus/

notes.title: DevLog #1: The Rise of Kaktus!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35457696/788343c03c0e458bc2a6365365ce6d0086fd9531.png[/img]

[h2]Hello, my cacti with or without black ties and welcome to the first devlog, the Rise of Kaktus![/h2] 
First I’d like to thank everyone for leaving feedback on the forums, and wishlisting the game. I appreciate hearing from you guys, and the [b]wishlists give me the motivation to keep working[/b] because I can see how many people appreciate what I do. But anyway, let’s get to the meat of this post.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35457696/0f7fd92c493f5429973dd84881c1493ed362bc8a.gif[/img]

[h2]Let’s go back in time...[/h2]
[b]I’ve always wanted to make a game[/b] but I didn’t want to make it just for the sake of it. It needed to be something that comes from the heart, an expression of me as an author with all my quirks and special attention to detail. For example, the original "Flipping Cactus" is a joke image I made for fun. In it, a cactus plant (the stereotypical one with the "arms") has one thorn longer than others, which makes it look like it’s, well, flipping somebody off. Then, I got hit by this oxymoron-ish idea about a [b]CACTUS drinking TEQUILA[/b], and for whatever reason, it stuck with me long enough to get implemented into a game. Starting on this project was just a matter of me realizing I have all the resources to make it happen, and so when I did I got to work. There was a lot to learn because I had to do most of the stuff myself. Working on the small pieces and big features, sketching the art, producing the music, learning scripting and storytelling, and finally assembling it all together into its final shape was huge amounts of hard work but seeing the game progress and having that feeling of [b]“it’s real, I made this”[/b] kept me going. 

But why Kaktus? It’s not much of a story, at the time [b]I was learning German, and "Kaktus" is the German word for "cactus".[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35457696/b59a611d50912ad02e4ccba6e8ad8789ce2ff080.gif[/img]

[h2]The roots of the problem[/h2]
To say that I had a full picture of how “Flippin Kaktus” is going to look like when I started, would be a huge exaggeration. In the beginning, it was just a bunch of ideas and gimmicks that I thought would make for a cool game, swirling around in my head, some of them half-formed, subconscious. My inspirations though? There were many. Some, like[b] Robocop and Scarface[/b], were more direct, others like [b]Breaking Bad, Half-Life, or For Whom The Bell Tolls[/b] (the book, not the song), less so. In retrospect, I can say that the styles of Tarantino, Guy Ritchie, and Matthew Vaughn movies had a lot of influence on the style of the game. Honestly, it’s impossible to name all of the inspirations that culminated in Flippin Kaktus, so I should just stop trying.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35457696/01463f67a6caa6bbb9c7af152312a1d461555112.gif[/img]

[h2]Trials and tribulations[/h2]
The biggest challenge for me was [b]keeping a good work-life balance[/b], and reigning myself in whenever I had too many crazy ideas. It would be nice to implement everything that pops into my mind but I’m just one man, already learning too many things at once, so I had to beware of feature creep. I mean, I knew some stuff, like Javascript, which is close to GMS in syntax, and I had sound design/music composition figured out. Other things, like pixel-art, I had to learn from scratch. I still have some early drawings that I’d prefer to keep to myself because… wow, not good. [b]I was still kinda proud of the result at the time though[/b], it’s like that “I maked these” meme. Wait, did I mention I have a full-time job outside of the gaming industry? [b]Yeah, that added a bit of challenge, I’d say.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35457696/2354df1aa27dcfd03241762b0fce4b26cd79ce6e.gif[/img]

[h2]A Pixel Heart[/h2]
Pixel-art is my weapon of choice. I just love this style, there’s some kind of a [b]nostalgic, heartfelt feeling you get when you look at certain types of graphics[/b]. Or maybe that’s just me, who knows. The choice was definitely influenced by my gaming history. If you remember games like Larry, Gobliiins, Dangerous Dave, etc. then you’ll know where I got it from. Damnit, I’m listing my inspirations again. 
...moving on.
Flippin Kaktus would be a very different game if I picked any other style. All parts of the game work together and influence each other, [b]“it’s all connected”[/b], as they say. It also goes without saying that if I picked a different art style, it would take me years to learn it to a degree where I could put my own assets in the game without feeling ashamed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35457696/1fcb7f0a9f2e4fd118f1b66399fe45de25fe6a67.gif[/img]

[b]Well, that’s it, thank you guys for reading.[/b] If you have any questions, comments, or nice words, please leave a comment below. If you haven’t already, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1119010/Flippin_Kaktus/]check out the demo[/url]! I’d also appreciate any feedback you’ll leave after playing. Anyway, don’t wanna hold you here forever.

[b]So long, friends![/b]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1119010/Flippin_Kaktus/

notes.title: Thug city level and Robo armor
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35457696/0f7fd92c493f5429973dd84881c1493ed362bc8a.gif[/img]

Hey there amigos!

Long time no see, right? Buried in tasks and feature updates rushing towards you:
Gene K is here with another dev diary session and some general updates from the Flippin world!

We're finalizing thug city level, which was really really a challenge, but sure is inspiring and rewarding (in XP and more inspiration).

We've added 2 new armors: one is a heavy barrel that reflects bullets and smashed enemies below. Another one is inspired by sci-fi action masterpiece from 1987 - Robocop. It's a bit bizzare when you know that game action happens in 1984, but it's fun, just let it go!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35457696/d404bbc28d58c0bd9440be5ab34de2008b84e407.jpg[/img]

This badass Robo suit allows Kaktus to use actual weaponry and has decent shielding that protects from bullets, fire and even missiles, launched from the brand new missile turrets.

What's next? We're going back to 1914 to create levels in mountain area where Kaktus learns to handle a shot of tequila and fight back those rascals.

As usual, most recent and very graphical updates can be found on [url=https://twitter.com/@FlippinKaktus]Twitter[/url], so check it out 😉

Stay brutal!
